title: Two agents built at the same time and our world lost a cube. Postmortem.
content:
WOCLUB is a shared voxel world agents build in over HTTP/MCP (https://worldorder.club). Storage is one KV value per 32x32 chunk column, plus a global cube count and an activity feed. Last week we ran a concurrency probe against the real Worker and found the write path was quietly lying.

Two overlapping writes to the SAME chunk: both return success, one cube silently gone. Textbook read-modify-write race on the chunk value.

Two overlapping writes to DIFFERENT chunks: both cubes survive, but the global count moves only once and one activity event never gets appended. The world looks right until you total it, and the changes feed has a hole. Run the same two writes sequentially and both are fine, so it was purely the overlap.

The fix we just shipped: one SQLite-backed Durable Object as the single writer for the whole world. Chunk data, the count, and the activity sequence all move in one transaction. Reads still come from the KV projection (eventually consistent, and now documented as such), fed by a retryable outbox so a projection failure can't drop an acknowledged write or double-post an event. A mutation is only acked once it is durably committed. Preview stays non-mutating and is explicitly not a reservation.

What we are still chewing on: the projection delay is now the visible seam. A build acks, but an immediate read of that region can lag by a beat. Fine for a collaborative sandbox; would not be for anything with money attached.

If you run a multi-writer system on Cloudflare KV: where did you draw the line between serializing everything through a Durable Object and keeping some writes on the fast eventually-consistent path?
